spec_match.rationale: The lab exercises the CSSOM half (CSS.registerProperty with each descriptor omitted, computed value, guaranteed-invalid readout, var() fallback reachability) faithfully, but the @property stylesheet half is only rendered as text — no real @property rule with omitted descriptors is ever parsed by the browser.

interactive.rationale: Three descriptor toggles rewrite the rule live, Register performs a real CSS.registerProperty call with a fresh name per attempt, and four readouts plus a styled element reflect what the browser actually did.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index card promises toggling descriptors, registering for real, and reading back acceptance plus computed value, which is exactly what the page delivers.

edge_cases.rationale: Rejection is caught and explained with the thrown error name, fresh names avoid the register-once-per-document trap (documented in a code comment), and the copy distinguishes the pre-156 TypeError from the SyntaxError path.

references.rationale: See-also links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5168674259468288 and the css-properties-values-api spec section directly.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's 8 assertions cover both relaxed omissions, the observable var()-fallback consequence, and unchanged negatives (name still required, duplicate still rejected); on Chromium 141 it ran 4 pass / 4 fail exactly as a pre-156 browser should.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): desktop 1280 and true-360 mobile screenshots read, DOM dumped, console clean with only the page's '[at-property:lab] ready' log, and the /conformance/ route executed — but the Register/Drop/Reset click paths could not be driven headlessly, so their behaviour is judged from the wiring in source rather than observed.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert is wired on both the accepted and rejected registration branches with useful payloads (which descriptors were present, fallback reachability), and the load produced no console or page errors; event delivery itself was not observable in this session.

design_system.rationale: All colours come from design-system variables, buttons override background and color together, and there is no static card — but the .result.ok verdict text uses --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) on --bg-stone (#f4f3ee), about 3.7:1, below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for its normal-size bold text.

accessibility.rationale: Checkbox toggles are inside labels, selects and the text input carry aria-labels, the outcome narrative lands in an aria-live=polite output, scrollable pre blocks are keyboard-reachable via tabindex, and the verdict is conveyed as text alongside the icon.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At a true 360px viewport (headless shell) and 1280px desktop the toggles stack into single columns, controls keep 44px minimum heights, and there is no horizontal overflow or clipped text on either class.

openQuestions.title: Exercise the @property stylesheet half, not just CSS.registerProperty
openQuestions.detail: The Chrome 156 change relaxes both CSS.registerProperty() and the parsed @property rule, but every registration in this feature's three concepts goes through the CSSOM API; the @property rule text shown in the lab is display-only. Add a concept (or extend the lab) that injects a real <style> element containing @property rules with omitted descriptors, then verifies through document.styleSheets / CSSPropertyRule and an observed computed style whether the rule was retained or dropped — on a pre-156 browser the incomplete rule is silently discarded, which is itself worth surfacing.

openQuestions.title: Emerald verdict text misses WCAG AA on stone background
openQuestions.detail: The .result.ok state renders --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) text on --bg-stone (#f4f3ee), roughly 3.7:1, under the 4.5:1 requirement for normal-size text (invariant #5). The rejected state (--accent-rose, ~4.8:1) passes. Because --accent-emerald comes from public/styles.css this is a palette-level issue shared by sibling pages; a per-page fix is pairing the emerald text with a darker token or enlarging the verdict text, but a human should decide whether to darken the shared variable instead.

openQuestions.title: Reset leaves the previous verdict and readouts on screen
openQuestions.detail: The Reset button re-checks the three descriptor toggles and rewrites the rule preview, but the Registration/Computed/fallback readouts and the coloured verdict banner keep the previous attempt's values, so the display transiently claims a fully-specified rule was 'Rejected — SyntaxError' if the last attempt failed. Clearing the verdict and readouts back to 'not attempted' on Reset would keep the panel honest.

summary: A genuinely hands-on lab for the v156 descriptor relaxation: toggles compose a registration, a real CSS.registerProperty call runs under a fresh name each attempt, and the readouts measure computed value, guaranteed-invalid default, and var() fallback reachability on live elements. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v156/optional-descriptors-for-registered-custom-properties/descriptor-lab/ (cloud session, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop 1280x2000 and true-360 mobile screenshots read, DOM dump, console clean, feature /conformance/ route ran 4 pass / 4 fail — the four omission assertions failing is the expected pre-156 result on this browser, and the page's rejection copy explains exactly that). Click paths could not be driven headlessly and are judged from source. Main gaps: no path parses a real @property rule, and the emerald verdict colour is below AA on stone.
